sequence: timelock (the token address, impersonated) → setPeerBridge(80002, 0x…080002) → peerBridges(80002) reads back
sender approve → initiateTransfer(token, 1e21, 80002, 0x…DEADBEEF) → tx 0x610bdee8… in fork block 44565, bridge balance 3.1e22

transferId taken from the TransferInitiated event topic1 = 0x042747ea2a5accec78a15b09a77e2b9494e78b03e82d4ac469fb31af704a8174 (recomputing it from the source formula silently gave the wrong value: transferId binds block.timestamp, and the fork's timestamp was not what the script assumed)
validator 1 signTransfer → signatureCount 1 → recipient still 0 (threshold not reached, nothing released)
validator 2 signTransfer → signatureCount 2 → _executeTransfer fires → recipient 1e21, bridge back to 3e22
guards: same validator twice → 'Already signed'; non-validator → 'Not authorized validator'; stranger initiate → ERC20InsufficientAllowance
quorumProofOnFork.notProven: the 'Transfer exists' duplicate guard. transferId includes block.timestamp, so an identical replay in a later block produces a different id and the guard is effectively unreachable — recorded instead of claimed.
quorumProofOnFork.conclusion: The multi-sig release path is functional with 3 registered validators and threshold 2. What is still missing is the INBOUND leg: _executeTransfer pays transfer.recipient from this bridge's balance on THIS chain, so a transfer destined for chain 80002 settles locally. That is the Phase-4 work.

sourceVerified.whyPartialMatch: Blockscout's standard-json route matches the deployed bytecode, which it records as partially_verified. The flattened-code route would set it false, but its controller has no viaIR parameter (grep of verification_controller.ex at v7.0.2: 0 hits), so a viaIR build cannot be reproduced there and would fail the bytecode comparison. Standard-json is therefore the only working route for this project.
caveats: Verification is async: the API answers {"message":"Smart-contract verification started"} and the row appears seconds later; poll /api/v2/smart-contracts/{address} for compiler_version.
The verifier must be able to write its compiler cache: the image runs as uid 1001 while a fresh named volume is root-owned, hence the sc-verifier-perms one-shot chown in the compose file.
source_code must be sent as the multipart field files[input] (a map). files[]=... makes Plug build a list, PublishHelper.prepare_files_array/1 returns [] and the API answers 'JSON files not found'.

sourceVerified.licenseTypeRootCause: SOLVED, and my earlier ERC-721/token-branch guess was wrong. The publish step dies on the multipart field license_type: 'MIT' -> changeset insert fails, 'none' -> publishes. Proof: LXONTOTPAuth is not a token, has no name/symbol/balanceOf in its ABI, and failed identically with MIT, then verified (compiler v0.8.26, 23 ABI entries) seconds later with none. Every contract in this batch went out with license_type=none. Consequence for the record's earlier note: nothing about Blockscout's token registration was involved, and nothing regressed at the HTTPS cutover — the two failed submissions were mine.

knownIssues: FIXED 2026-10-21 and redeployed: LXONStakingEnhanced.unstake(uint256) could never succeed on v1 (0x37e1c5eC…) — the noFlashLoan modifier requires the contract's token balance not to drop, and paying the payout out is unstake's only effect, so every exit reverted 'Flash loan detected'. v2 at 0x4645Fd49… takes the modifier off unstake, sends the early-unstake penalty to treasury, and clears stakeOwner so the stake NFT really burns. Proven live: stake 1000e18 -> unstake -> contract balance 0, treasury +100e18, ownerOf(0)=0 (txs 0x571535d6… / 0x50e8e30b…). 1000 LXON stays trapped in the v1 address; no function can move it, and v1 is unrecoverable.

Live bridge now has 3 registered validators at 10,000 LXON each (blocks 44515-44522) and the sign-to-release quorum is proven on a fork of the real bytecode. Two things remain true: no peer bridge is registered on production, so initiateTransfer still reverts 'Chain not registered'; and even with a peer, _executeTransfer pays the recipient on this chain, so the destination-chain leg does not exist yet. A placeholder peer was deliberately NOT scheduled through the 48h timelock — it would enable a mechanism whose release semantics are wrong and put real deposits behind them.

Two tokens named LXON coexist: LXONNativeToken (symbol XON, 100M, no roles) at 0xe801… and LxonTokenEnhanced (symbol LXON, now 100M, AccessControl+Permit+Timelock) at 0x9980…. Pick one before any wallet or dApp integration, or rename one.

Bridge release semantics are single-chain only. signTransfer → _executeTransfer pays the recipient from this bridge's own balance; there is no inbound claim path (no completeTransfer/mint-on-verify), so a real second chain would need one. The `toChainId == block.chainid` guard that used to block the flow was removed rather than reworked — see the comment in _executeTransfer.

Deployer keeps MINTER_ROLE on LxonTokenEnhanced after the supply correction (it also holds DEFAULT_ADMIN, so it could re-grant itself). For a production token, minting belongs behind the timelock or a multisig.
Three bridge deployments are live at once (0xbc18…, 0xb4927a…, 0x28c93c…). Only 0x28c93c… holds token roles; treat the other two as dead code that is still source-verified and discoverable.

Dead path discovered while wiring the device cluster: LXONPhygitalBridge.activatePhygital calls lxonToken.mintEcosystemReward(protocolAuthority, bonus, "phygital_activation"), but the deployed LXONNativeToken at 0xe801… exposes only transfer/approve/transferFrom/mint/burn/allowance/balanceOf/totalSupply/decimals/name/symbol/owner/INITIAL_SUPPLY/MAX_SUPPLY/transferOwnership (21-entry verified ABI, and mintEcosystemReward exists only in the undeployed LXONNativeToken.sol:491). So the activation bonus reverts; activation additionally needs a chip registered with a founder TOTP code. Token-bound hardware-wallet flow is therefore deployable but not yet functional end to end.

Superseded, not deleted: LXONWrapper v1 (0x76EF2514…) is still on chain and still lets any caller mint unlimited wLXON with no collateral, because wrap() never touched originalLXON. Fixed in code and redeployed as v2 (0xC0CF6B0E6C5a0705F319BA5c629a6Bc7E82FEf00); v1 holds 0 LXON with 0 supply and 0 holders, so no funds moved, but the address stays discoverable and must not be listed anywhere.

Two tokens are now wired into two clusters each: the device cluster (phygital bridge, hardware wallet, TB account) is pinned to LXONNativeToken 0xe801… (symbol XON) because LXONPhygitalBridge/LXONHardwareWallet declare the state var as type LXONNativeToken; the finance cluster (validator staking, slashing, vesting, wrapper, staking v2) uses LxonTokenEnhanced 0x9980… (symbol LXON). The 'pick one before any wallet listing' issue is now load-bearing, not theoretical.

Not deployed: LXONCrossChainRouter (no LayerZero endpoint on 724 and no LayerZero package in lib/), LXONGovernanceHardened (wants an IVotes token; LxonTokenEnhanced is not one), the DEX/peg/price cluster (needs mock USDC/WETH + a self-funded pair to 'work' — declined 2026-10-21), 4 competing bridge rewrites, and the duplicate/test tokens.

Deliberate remaining hole in LXONWrapper v2: mint()/burnFrom() are MINTER_ROLE-gated and the deployer holds that role, so the admin can still print wLXON that this contract does not custody — legitimate only for wLXONBridge's custody-at-the-bridge model, which is not deployed. The BRIDGE_ROLE restriction that would close it was offered and not taken; it costs nothing to add now because supply is 0.
resolvedIssues: 2026-10-19: token.executeTimelock() reverted against the bridge (bridge setters required DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, which the token never held). Fixed by gating the five parameter setters on an immutable timelock address instead of granting the token admin rights.

2026-10-19: LXONBridgeEnhanced declared TIMELOCK_ADMIN and TIMELOCK_DELAY but enforced neither. Setters are now actually delayed 48h through LxonTokenEnhanced; TIMELOCK_ADMIN on the bridge is documented as vestigial (it grants nothing).

2026-10-19: addValidator/removeValidator/slashValidator did IERC20(address(this)).safeTransferFrom/safeTransfer although the bridge holds no token, so all three reverted with 'Address with no code'. The bridge now takes an immutable lxonToken and the path was exercised on chain (1e22 staked and returned).

2026-10-19: signTransfer could never release a transfer — _executeTransfer required status Pending while every initiate path stored Locked. It now requires Locked and the multi-sig tests that were skipped for this pass.

2026-10-19: 6-vs-18 decimal mismatch. Convention fixed as 18 decimals; LxonTokenEnhanced totalSupply minted from 1e14 to 1e26 (100,000,000 LXON), and LXONStakingEnhanced MIN_STAKE/MAX_STAKE changed from *1e6 to *1e18.

2026-10-19: testGasSavingsPermitVsApprove panicked on `gasApprove - gasPermit` underflow and the permit tests signed for an address no key controlled. Both fixed; the unsupported 'permit is cheaper per call' assertion was removed.

2026-10-20: the public RPC was a chain-takeover vector — Besu exposed ADMIN/QBFT/MINER on 0.0.0.0:8545 with a world security-group rule, and on a QBFT n=1/f=0 chain a single anonymous qbft_proposeValidatorVote makes the caller a validator. Remediated: loopback-only port publishing, both SG rules revoked, API set trimmed to ETH,NET,WEB3,DEBUG,TXPOOL,TRACE, host allowlist pinned to localhost/127.0.0.1/besu-sealer, wildcard CORS dropped, and the explorer's advertised wallet RPC (JSON_RPC / NEXT_PUBLIC_NETWORK_RPC_URL) emptied. foundry.toml's `lxon` endpoint is now http://127.0.0.1:8545 behind an SSH tunnel.

2026-10-21: LXONWrapper's unbacked wrap/unwrap. wrap() now escrows LXON via SafeERC20 before minting, unwrap() burns then returns it 1:1, the declared DECIMALS = 6 constant contradicts the runtime 18 it was replaced with a decimals() override, and the no-redemption burn(uint256) was removed. Written test-first in test/WrapperCollateral.t.sol (5 of 7 tests fail against v1 before the change), redeployed at 0xC0CF6B0E… in block 44335, source-verified, and proved on chain with a 500 LXON wrap→unwrap round trip that left the caller's balance byte-identical.

2026-10-21: minConfirmations=2 guarded nothing because validatorsRegistered was 0. Three validators registered with 1e22 stake each; VALIDATOR_ROLE granted to all three; quorum mechanics proven on a fork (see verified.LXONBridgeEnhanced.quorumProofOnFork).
